![](careing-for-data_banner.jpg){fig-alt="Abstract blue waves" width="100%"}

Research data in the humanities and social sciences is rarely simply "open" or "closed". Much of
it describes people — their words, their images, their suffering — and caring for such data is a
question of ethics as much as of infrastructure. The **CARE principles** (Collective benefit,
Authority to control, Responsibility, Ethics) put those questions beside the FAIR ones, and the
seventh edition of "… in dialogue" asks what that looks like in practice.

Researchers bring **concrete datasets** to the table and discuss the ethical questions each one
raises, in short pitches, hands-on sessions and with perspectives from law.

**9 December 2026 · Kuppelraum (501), Hochschulstrasse 4, University of Bern · in English · hybrid**

## On the programme

- **Keynote** — *Beyond FAIR: CARE, Community Responsibility, and the Challenges of (Historical)
  Sociolinguistic Data*, Anita Auer (University of Lausanne), on pauper letters and Swiss Heritage
  Tamil
- **Dataset pitches** on psychiatric patient letters, witch-trial records, ethnographic fieldwork,
  a discrimination-sensitive scholarly edition, archaeological site data, emergency-medicine
  records and research on sexual abuse in the Catholic Church
- **Hands-on sessions** on discrimination-sensitive metadata, and a "bring your own data" slot
- A closing contribution from **CCdigitallaw** on how open research data can be, and at what cost

The full programme, all abstracts and short biographies are on the
[event page](/content/events/im_dialog/2026-careing-for-data-in-dialogue/).

## Registration

Registration is free and runs through the University Library Bern — see the event page, or share
the short link **<https://bit.ly/imdialog2026>**. The
[flyer is available as a PDF](careing-for-data-in-dialogue-flyer.pdf) for printing and
circulating.

The workshop is organised by the Digital Humanities Center at the Walter Benjamin Kolleg and
Open Science at the University Library Bern. Questions go to
[imdialog\@ub.unibe.ch](mailto:imdialog@ub.unibe.ch).
